directAnswer: To stop your TV from turning on with your console, disable HDMI-CEC on the console or the TV. This feature is often branded differently depending on the manufacturer, such as Bravia Sync, Anynet+, or SIMPLINK.
summary: HDMI-CEC allows devices to control each other via HDMI, which can lead to your TV turning on when you power up a console. Disabling this feature on the device that initiates the power-on command can resolve the issue.

sections.heading: Understanding HDMI-CEC
sections.body: HDMI-CEC (Consumer Electronics Control) is a protocol that allows HDMI devices to control each other. It can automatically turn on your TV and switch inputs when a connected device, like a console, is powered on. Different brands have unique names for this feature, such as Sony's Bravia Sync and Samsung's Anynet+.

sections.heading: Disabling HDMI-CEC
sections.body: To prevent your TV from turning on with your console, you can disable HDMI-CEC on the console, TV, or any intermediary device like a soundbar. This stops the automatic power-on command from being sent.

steps.title: Disable HDMI-CEC on the console
steps.detail: For PS5: Go to Settings → System → HDMI → turn off Enable HDMI Device Link. For Xbox: Navigate to Profile & system → Settings → General → TV & display options → Advanced → turn off HDMI-CEC (Device control). For Nintendo Switch: Go to System Settings → TV Settings → turn off Match TV Power State.

steps.title: Disable HDMI-CEC on the TV
steps.detail: Access the TV’s settings menu, usually under HDMI or External inputs, and disable HDMI-CEC or its branded equivalent like Bravia Sync, Anynet+, or SIMPLINK. Look for options like Auto power on or Power on with HDMI.

steps.title: Check intermediary devices
steps.detail: If your setup includes a soundbar or AVR, ensure HDMI-CEC is disabled there as well. These devices can also send power-on commands to the TV.

steps.title: Test with different HDMI inputs
steps.detail: Try connecting your console to a different HDMI port on the TV, as some ports may have CEC enabled by default. This can help isolate the issue.

faqs.question: Can I still use my TV remote to control console volume?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can often disable power-on linking while keeping HDMI control for volume. This depends on your TV's settings.

faqs.question: Why does my TV switch inputs when I turn on the console?
faqs.answer: This is part of the HDMI-CEC feature called one-touch play. Disabling HDMI-CEC will stop both the power-on and input switching.

caveats: Some TVs may re-enable HDMI-CEC after a firmware update, so check settings if the issue reoccurs.
Disabling HDMI-CEC will not affect picture quality or features like 4K or 120Hz.
